name: Earth-observation analytics
summary: Satellite imagery combined with geospatial software and AI turns repeated observations of Earth into useful alerts, measurements and operational decisions.
useCase: A utility monitors vegetation near power lines, while an insurer checks flood exposure and a food company follows crop conditions across its supply chain.
whyNow: The commercial shift is from purchasing isolated images to recurring monitoring services linked to an operational workflow. Planet’s revenue rose from $113.2 million in fiscal 2021 to $307.7 million in fiscal 2026, a company-level demand proxy. Fiscal 2026 ended on 31 January 2026 and must not be confused with calendar 2026. Later, its quarter ended July 2026 produced $116.1 million, but that quarterly value is kept separate from annual history. Sensor diversity, more frequent revisits and analytics can improve useful coverage. The limiting factors are often accuracy, latency, integration, ground-truth validation and whether an alert changes a customer decision.

mainstream.scope: Routine automated satellite monitoring in selected utility, agriculture, insurance, environmental and government workflows that have measurable decision value.
mainstream.rationale: Commercial data subscriptions already exist and analytics reduce the specialist effort needed to use them. Integration and validation can make recurring monitoring routine in more vertical markets by the late 2020s. This does not imply continuous, equally accurate coverage of every asset; cloud cover, resolution, revisit time and economics remain use-case constraints.

milestones.text: Planet’s fiscal year ended January 2021 recorded $113.168 million revenue; the metric uses fiscal labels.
Planet reported fiscal revenue of $131.209 million.
Fiscal revenue reached about $191.3 million; this is a company proxy, not a whole-market census.
Planet fiscal revenue reached about $220.7 million.
Planet fiscal revenue was $244.352 million. Maxar Intelligence rebranded to Vantor later in the calendar year, and IonQ acquired Capella Space.
Planet reported FY2026 revenue of $307.727 million and later $116.1 million for the quarter ended July 31. Its September annual guidance is still a forecast.

tailwinds: Recurring monitoring can help customers manage climate, infrastructure and supply-chain risks.
Cloud geospatial tools and machine learning reduce the manual effort of extracting useful measurements.
Combining optical, radar and specialised sensors can address complementary needs.
bottlenecks: A model needs reliable validation for each geography, season and operating condition.
Resolution, revisit time, clouds and tasking constraints limit some use cases.
Customer integration, licensing and data acquisition costs can dominate model cost.
watchMetrics: Recurring commercial revenue and retention, separated from one-off government or satellite contracts.
Alert accuracy, false-positive rate, observation-to-decision latency and validated customer savings.
Usable revisits and sensor coverage at the price the customer actually pays.
